I see. Then it is due to the estimator. To mu understanding, BIC needs the log likelilhood (though model chi-square can be used as a proxy in ML). With ULS, the log likelihood is not available and so maybe BIC cannot be computed?

# Using the cfa example:
> logLik(fit)
'log Lik.' NA (df=21)
Warning message:
In logLik(fit) : lavaan WARNING: logLik only available if estimator is ML

You can try GLS and you should find that BIC is also not available.

-- Shu Fai
